notes_for_editor: Disagreements stated in the text, not resolved: original tower height (NRHP 89 ft; HistoryLink 91 ft/100 ft above sea level; USLHS 89 ft; Lighthouse Friends 92 ft, not cited); fog bell weight (1,100 vs 1,200 lb); keepers' house cost (NRHP $45,000 vs HistoryLink ~$5,000) and year (1904/1905); amount removed in 1927 (NRHP 26 and 27 ft; Lighthouse Friends about 30 ft); lens fitted 1927 (NRHP: from Admiralty Head; HistoryLink: origin unknown); Boyling/Blake head-keeper dates 1858-60; Morgan first name (NRHP 'Amos'; USLHS 'Osmore H.'; Lighthouse Friends gives 1882-96); automation 1975 vs 1976; diaphone date (NRHP 1937, HistoryLink 1940, Lighthouse Friends 1937 - not used). Not used: Lighthouse Friends says the second assistant post was abolished after 1934 electrification, but USLHS lists second assistants to 1941. NRHP prints the 1874 wreck as 'Chrisptopher Mitchell' (OCR/typo); I wrote Christopher. The nomination was OCR'd and quotes in evidence keep its OCR errors. The 1868 massacre account rests on HistoryLink (Creative Commons, itself from secondary books) and was not checked against the Jamestown S'Klallam Tribe's own account (jamestowntribe.org/history/hist_massacre.htm); a reviewer may want to add it or the Curtis 1913 account. HistoryLink's Blake couple details (marriage date, census) are second-hand from census/local histories. Roster comes from USLHS (NARA registers); 'USCG' rows are kept as 'other' and include 1960s-1980 Coast Guard personnel as the archive prints them. Bulletin quotes (1914, 1923, 1929) are from OCR; I did not look at page images, and PDF page numbers come from the corpus tool's page labels. 1923 Bulletin: the fire is dated 14-15 October in the text, issue month not checked. Newspapers.py was not used; the station has HistoryLink-cited Seattle Times articles (Oct 9 and 13, 1914 on the Sioux) that a later pass could read. The Corpus holds Light-House Board reports only for 1891-1901, so 1873 whistle appropriation, the 1904 dwelling appropriation and the 1927 lowering rest on the NRHP and HistoryLink.
